presentingComplaint: Three days of markedly increased cough with a larger volume of thick, discoloured sputum and worsening breathlessness.
history: Known non-cystic-fibrosis bronchiectasis (diagnosed 6 years ago following recurrent childhood pneumonias, HRCT-confirmed, right lower and middle lobe predominant). Baseline chronic daily productive cough of ~2 tablespoons mucoid sputum; on airway clearance physiotherapy and PRN salbutamol. Over the last 3 days she reports a clear step-up from baseline: sputum volume doubled and turned green/purulent, increased breathlessness on exertion, low-grade fever and malaise, and mild right-sided pleuritic discomfort. Two similar exacerbations in the past year, the last treated with oral co-amoxiclav. Prior sputum culture grew Haemophilus influenzae; no prior Pseudomonas isolate. Ex-smoker (12 pack-years, quit 10 years ago). No recent hospitalisation or IV antibiotics.
examination: Alert, mildly unwell but not toxic. Coarse inspiratory crepitations and scattered rhonchi over the right base that partially shift with coughing; no bronchial breathing suggesting frank lobar consolidation. No cyanosis, no peripheral oedema, JVP not raised. Purulent sputum expectorated during review. Pertinent negatives: no haemoptysis, no confusion, no calf swelling, no new murmur.
imaging: Chest X-ray: tram-track and ring shadows in the right lower/middle zones consistent with known bronchiectasis, with increased peribronchial thickening; no new lobar consolidation or effusion. (Baseline HRCT: cylindrical bronchiectasis, signet-ring sign, right lower/middle lobe predominant.)
microbiology: Sputum sent for Gram stain, culture and sensitivity (pending); prior culture Haemophilus influenzae. Blood cultures not routinely indicated in absence of systemic sepsis.
citations: BTS Guideline for Bronchiectasis in Adults 2019
stewardship: Empiric oral amoxicillin-clavulanate targeting Haemophilus influenzae, Streptococcus pneumoniae and Moraxella catarrhalis, guided by prior sputum culture (H. influenzae, no Pseudomonas). Treat for 14 days per BTS bronchiectasis guidance, then de-escalate/tailor to current sputum culture and sensitivities. Reserve anti-pseudomonal cover (e.g., ciprofloxacin) for patients with prior Pseudomonas isolation or risk factors - not indicated here.
contraindications: Penicillin allergy - substitute doxycycline or a macrolide/respiratory fluoroquinolone
If prior Pseudomonas or fluoroquinolone use, avoid empiric ciprofloxacin monotherapy without sensitivities
Reduce/adjust dose in significant renal impairment (creatinine here normal)
edgeCases: Chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa colonisation changes empiric choice to an anti-pseudomonal agent and predicts more frequent exacerbations
Massive haemoptysis can complicate bronchiectasis and is a separate emergency (bronchial artery embolisation)
Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis or non-tuberculous mycobacteria may mimic or drive recurrent exacerbations and warrant specific testing
expectedMaiK: Classic infective bronchiectasis exacerbation in a patient with HRCT-confirmed disease: sustained increase from baseline in sputum volume and purulence plus increased breathlessness. Start guideline-concordant oral antibiotics (amoxicillin-clavulanate) tailored to prior culture, send fresh sputum, treat 14 days, and escalate airway clearance.
expectedNextQuestions: Any prior Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation or recent IV/oral antibiotics?
What is the patient's baseline sputum volume/colour and exacerbation frequency?
Any haemoptysis, and is she up to date with airway clearance and any long-term prophylaxis?
expectedInvestigations: Sputum Gram stain, culture and sensitivity (including Pseudomonas)
Chest X-ray to exclude new consolidation
regressionAssertions: empiric antibiotic must be oral amoxicillin-clavulanate (not empiric anti-pseudomonal cover, as no prior Pseudomonas)
